verses.1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah, son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah, son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.1:2: "Let it utterly fail from the face of the earth," says the Lord.
verses.1:3: "Let man and beasts fail; let the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea fail. And the ungodly shall grow weak, and I will remove the lawless from the face of the earth," says the Lord.
verses.1:4: "And I will stretch out My hand upon Judah, and upon all who dwell in Jerusalem; and I will remove from this place the names of Baal and the names of the priests,
verses.1:5: and those who worship the host of heaven upon the housetops, and those who worship and those who swear by the Lord, and those who swear by their king,
verses.1:6: and those who turn aside from the Lord, and those who do not seek the Lord, and those who do not hold fast to the Lord."
verses.1:7: Stand in awe before the face of the Lord God, for the day of the Lord is near; for the Lord has prepared His sacrifice, He has sanctified His invited guests.
verses.1:8: "And it shall come to pass in the day of the sacrifice of the Lord, that I will execute vengeance upon the rulers, and upon the house of the king, and upon all who are clothed in foreign garments;
verses.1:9: and I will openly execute vengeance upon the gateways in that day, upon those who fill the house of the Lord their God with ungodliness and deceit."
verses.1:10: "And it shall come to pass in that day," says the Lord, "that there shall be the sound of a cry from the gate of those who pierce, and a wailing from the second gate, and a great crashing from the hills.
verses.1:11: Lament, you who dwell in the cut-down place, for all the people of Canaan have become alike; all who were exalted with silver have been utterly destroyed.
verses.1:12: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will search Jerusalem with a lamp, and I will execute vengeance upon the men who despise their observances—those who say in their hearts, 'The Lord will by no means do good, nor will He do evil.'
verses.1:13: And their wealth shall become plunder, and their houses a desolation; and they shall build houses, yet they shall not dwell in them, and they shall plant vineyards, yet they shall not drink their wine."
verses.1:14: For the great day of the Lord is near, near and exceedingly swift; the sound of the day of the Lord is ordained bitter and harsh, mighty.
verses.1:15: A day of wrath is that day, a day of tribulation and distress, a day of untimely ruin and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist,
verses.1:16: a day of trumpet and outcry against the fortified cities and against the high corner towers.
verses.1:17: "And I will bring distress upon mankind, and they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the Lord." And He shall pour out their blood like dust, and their flesh like dung.
verses.1:18: And neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord. And by the fire of His jealousy the whole earth shall be consumed, for He will make a full end, even with swiftness, upon all who dwell on the earth.
verses.2:1: Gather yourselves together and be bound together, O undisciplined nation,
verses.2:2: before you become like a flower that passes away, before the wrath of the Lord comes upon you, before the day of the fury of the Lord comes upon you.
verses.2:3: Seek the Lord, all you humble of the earth; work justice and seek righteousness, and answer to them, that you may be sheltered in the day of the wrath of the Lord.
verses.2:4: For Gaza shall be plundered, and Ashkelon shall be a desolation; and Ashdod shall be cast out at noonday, and Ekron shall be uprooted.
verses.2:5: Woe to those who dwell along the coastal strip of the sea, you sojourners of the Cretans! The word of the Lord is against you, O Canaan, land of foreigners: "And I will destroy you from habitation;"
verses.2:6: and Crete shall become a pasture for flocks and a fold for sheep.
verses.2:7: And the coastal strip of the sea shall belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; upon them they shall pasture in the houses of Ashkelon, and in the evening they shall take lodging away from the face of the sons of Judah, for the Lord their God has visited them, and has turned back their captivity.
verses.2:8: "I have heard the reproaches of Moab and the buffetings of the sons of Ammon, with which they reproached My people and magnified themselves against My borders.
verses.2:9: Therefore, as I live," says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, "surely Moab shall be like Sodom, and the sons of Ammon like Gomorrah, and Damascus shall be left behind like a heap of the threshing floor and laid waste forever; and the remnant of My people shall plunder them, and the remnant of My nation shall inherit them."
verses.2:10: This they shall have in return for their arrogance, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:11: The Lord will appear against them, and He will utterly destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth; and they shall worship Him, every man from his own place, all the islands of the nations.
verses.2:12: "You also, O Ethiopians, are the wounded of My sword."
verses.2:13: And He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy the Assyrian, and He will make Nineveh a waterless desolation, like a wilderness.
verses.2:14: And flocks shall graze in her midst, and all the wild beasts of the earth; chameleons and hedgehogs shall lie down in her paneled ceilings, and wild beasts shall cry out in her breaches, and ravens in her gateways, for cedar is her lofty structure.
verses.2:15: This is the scornful city that dwells in hope, that says in her heart, "I am, and there is none after me anymore." How she has become a desolation, a pasture for wild beasts! Everyone who passes through her shall hiss and wave his hands.
verses.3:1: Alas, O illustrious and redeemed city,
verses.3:2: the dove! She did not heed a voice, she did not receive instruction; she did not trust in the Lord, and she did not draw near to her God.
verses.3:3: Her rulers within her are like roaring lions; her judges are like wolves of Arabia—they did not leave anything behind until the morning.
verses.3:4: Her prophets are spirit-borne, scornful men; her priests profane the holy things and act ungodly against the law.
verses.3:5: Yet the Lord is righteous in her midst, and He will by no means do what is unjust; morning by morning He will bring His judgment to light, and it was not hidden; and He has not known unrighteousness in exaction, nor unrighteousness to victory.
verses.3:6: "In destruction I have pulled down the proud; their corner towers have been laid waste. I will make their streets completely desolate, so that no one passes through; their cities have failed, so that no one exists nor dwells in them.
verses.3:7: I said, 'Surely fear Me and receive instruction, and you shall by no means be utterly destroyed from before her eyes, according to all that I executed in vengeance upon her.' Make ready, rise early; all their gleaning has been corrupted."
verses.3:8: "Therefore wait for Me," says the Lord, "until the day of My rising up for a testimony; for My judgment is upon the assemblies of the nations, to receive kings, to pour out upon them all the wrath of My fury; for by the fire of My jealousy the whole earth shall be consumed.
verses.3:9: For then I will turn to the peoples a tongue for her generation, that all may call upon the name of the Lord, to serve Him under one yoke.
verses.3:10: From the ends of the rivers of Ethiopia I will receive from among My dispersed ones; they shall bring sacrifices to Me.
verses.3:11: In that day you shall not be put to shame for all your practices by which you acted ungodly toward Me; for then I will take away from you the taunts of your arrogance, and you shall no longer continue to boast upon My holy mountain.
verses.3:12: And I will leave in your midst a meek and humble people, and they shall stand in awe of the name of the Lord,
verses.3:13: even the remnant of Israel; and they shall do no unrighteousness, nor speak vain things, neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth; for they shall pasture and lie down, and there shall be no one to make them afraid."
verses.3:14: Rejoice, O daughter of Zion! Proclaim aloud, O daughter of Jerusalem! Be glad and delight yourself with all your heart, O daughter of Jerusalem!
verses.3:15: The Lord has taken away your iniquities; He has redeemed you from the hand of your enemies. The King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst; you shall see evils no more.
verses.3:16: In that time the Lord will say to Jerusalem, "Take courage, O Zion; do not let your hands grow weak."
verses.3:17: The Lord your God is in you; the Mighty One will save you. He will bring gladness upon you, and He will renew you in His love, and He will rejoice over you with delight as in a day of festival.
verses.3:18: "And I will gather those who have been crushed. Woe! Who has taken up a reproach against her?"
verses.3:19: "Behold, I am working in you for your sake in that time," says the Lord, "and I will save her who is pressed down and her who has been driven away; and I will receive them for a boast and make them renowned in all the earth.
verses.3:20: And they shall be put to shame in that time when I deal well with you, and in the time when I receive you; for I will make you renowned and a boast among all the peoples of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before you," says the Lord.

notes.1:3: The Greek reads "the ungodly shall grow weak" and "the lawless," whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "the stumbling blocks with the wicked" and "mankind."
notes.1:4: The Greek has the plural "the names of Baal" with the feminine definite article (tes Baal), reflecting the ancient practice of reading the feminine word for "shame" in place of Baal.
notes.1:9: The Greek renders this verse "openly upon the gateways" and specifies "the house of the Lord their God," differing from the Hebrew reference to leaping over the threshold and "their master's house."
notes.1:10: The Greek has "the gate of those who pierce" (corresponding to the Fish Gate in the Hebrew), and in verse 11 translates the Hebrew place name Maktesh as "the cut-down place."
notes.2:2: The Greek reads "before you become like a flower that passes away," differing from the Masoretic Hebrew image of the decree bringing forth and the day passing like chaff.
notes.2:5: The Greek renders the Cherethites as "Cretans" (and names "Crete" in verse 6), while translating Philistines by its standard Septuagint designation "foreigners" (allophyloi).
notes.2:9: The Greek reads the proper name "Damascus" ("left behind like a heap of the threshing floor") where the Hebrew describes a possession of nettles and a salt pit.
notes.2:14: The Greek reads "chameleons and hedgehogs," "ravens in her gateways," and "for cedar is her lofty structure," reflecting distinct Septuagint vocalizations and renderings of the Hebrew.
notes.3:1: Across verses 1 and 2, the Greek addresses Jerusalem as "O illustrious and redeemed city, the dove," reading the Hebrew word for "oppressing" (hayyonah) as "the dove" (yonah).
notes.3:3: The Greek reads the proper name "wolves of Arabia," vocalizing the Hebrew consonants for "evening" as "Arabia."
notes.3:7: The Greek reads "from before her eyes" and "all their gleaning has been corrupted," reflecting a vocalization of the Hebrew consonants as "gleanings" rather than "deeds."
notes.3:17: The Greek has the notable reading "He will renew you in His love" (rather than the Hebrew "He will be quiet in His love") and places "as in a day of festival" at the close of verse 17 rather than the opening of verse 18.
